items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And my sextet included ... and of course the great Billy Hart on multiple percussion.

ctx.x: All right. I like the way you describe your own music as two flowers and a stem. Can you elaborate on that for me?

Well yeah. Two flowers on a stem is a metaphor expressing the symbiotic relationship of my cultural identity as a Chinese-American and a way of honoring tradition and encouraging new ideas, new innovation. “Two Flowers on a Stem” is also the name of a work that I composed I think in the early nineties and it’s the title track of the Jon Jang sextet on Soul Note Records, which is a company that’s based in Milano, Italy and a recording company incidentally that promoted a lot of David Murray’s work. And my sextet…

was the period of the McCarthy period. And if you were a Chinese-American you were suspicious of being a Communist and so forth. I actually had an FBI investigation, but mainly because he worked for the chemical plants and so he received Q Clearance, which was the highest clearance. But anyway he died in this plane crash in 1956, a two airplane crash. And when my family tried to hold services at the Glendale Cemetery I think — was it in Burbank or Glendale — I was only two years old — they refused us services.…
